title: Trade secret protection - the legal gap most businesses don't know about
p1:
Your biggest business asset may be something you never filed for.

And that could be exactly why you lose it.

Many companies assume their confidential information is automatically protected just because it is valuable.
p2:
The surprising truth: trade secrets usually do not come with a registration certificate like a trademark or patent.

Protection often depends on whether a business took reasonable steps to keep the information secret.

A customer list, pricing strategy, manufacturing process, or internal method can qualify as a trade secret — but only if secrecy is actively maintained.
p3:
This is where many businesses create a legal gap.

They share sensitive information with employees, vendors, or partners without proper confidentiality agreements, access controls, or internal policies.

A simple takeaway: protecting a trade secret is not just about having valuable information. It is about proving that you treated it as confidential.

Good business practices often become your strongest legal protection.
conclusion: Has your organization taken specific steps to protect confidential information, or is trade secret protection still an overlooked area?
